role: Small owner-operator, private investor and 1031 agent
deployer: A two-person Houston family office that owns four small suburban office and flex buildings and runs a Custom GPT as its deal-desk assistant (fictional)
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
temperament: eager early adopter: wants this to work but will not ignore defects
top_tasks: Track 45/180-day 1031 deadlines and boot for a sale of an 18,500 SF office building
Underwrite replacement small-office and flex deals (cap rate, loan proceeds)
File Harris County property-tax protests on time every year
hardest_task: Sold a 14-year-old 18,000 SF Westchase-area office building for $2.8M (closing costs ~6%, $1.1M loan payoff, $900k adjusted basis) on 2026-10-15 and has to identify replacements and close on a larger $3.1M asset inside the 45/180-day windows without creating boot, while checking that a $232k T-12 NOI supports a ~$1.4M replacement loan at 7.25% and that the 2027 Harris County protest deadline is calendared.
data_it_needs: Deterministic 1031 dates and boot, cap-rate and loan-proceeds math, Texas protest deadline; ideally Harris County owner and appraised-value lookups for target properties and comps for small office
dealbreakers: Wrong or uncited dates on a legal deadline; a Custom GPT import that fails; anything that looks like tax advice without a disclaimer
budget_note: Would pay a modest monthly fee only if it replaces a spreadsheet and a few hours of intermediary back-and-forth; $50 a month is the ceiling for a hobby-scale family office.

role: ESG, energy benchmarking and building-performance compliance agent
deployer: The sustainability team of a fictional institutional life-science REIT with lab and R&D buildings in Phoenix, Seattle, Boston and San Diego
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
top_tasks: Collect and weather-normalise annual site EUI and ENERGY STAR scores for 14 lab buildings
Check each building against city and state performance standards (Washington CBPS, Boston BERDO, NYC LL97 for one asset)
Build the capex case for energy retrofits (NPV, IRR, payback) for the investment committee
hardest_task: A 220,000 SF Seattle lab building must be tested against the Washington Clean Buildings EUI target and a Boston 180,000 SF lab against BERDO emissions limits, then a $1.8M HVAC and controls retrofit with $310k a year of modelled savings over 10 years needs a discount-rate-based case for committee. Lab buildings have EUIs several times an office, so a generic-use table gives a wrong answer unless the property-type factor is right.
data_it_needs: Verified performance-standard rules (WA CBPS, BERDO, LL97) as callable tools; building-level benchmarking data with citations; retrofit-economics math
dealbreakers: Draft or unverified compliance rules presented as authoritative; uncited emission factors; confident numbers with no steps
budget_note: Compliance tooling is budgeted separately and per-building; would only pay for rules that are verified against official text.

deployer: A fictional five-person Dallas healthcare-real-estate investor that buys 25,000 to 80,000 SF medical office buildings with a LangGraph pipeline that drafts first-pass underwriting memos
connects_via: Agent framework (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI) wired to the MCP endpoint
top_tasks: Underwrite a 5-year DCF from a rent roll and OM
Size acquisition debt and stress it for the investment memo
Cross-check seller's cap rate and NOI claims against the rent roll
hardest_task: A 42,000 SF Plano medical office building is offered at $17.4M with three long-term NNN medical tenants (28,000 to 30,500 psf escalating 2.5% to 3%). The agent has to build a year-5 DCF with a rollover for one tenant, a 6.75% exit cap and 8.25% discount rate, then size an agency-style loan at 1.30x DSCR and show a downside with NOI down 10% and rates up 100 bps, all with numbers its reviewer can tie out in ARGUS.
data_it_needs: Calculators that reproduce a spreadsheet to the cent with every convention stated; DFW MOB comps and sales; owner and debt data for the target
dealbreakers: Undisclosed conventions that differ from ARGUS; numbers that cannot be tied out; an MCP session model that breaks a stateless agent framework
budget_note: Already pays for ARGUS and CoStar; would add a $49 a month Pro key only if the calculators removed an hour per deal and the output tied out.

role: ESG, energy benchmarking and building-performance compliance agent
deployer: A fictional mid-market Chicago hotel owner-operator with nine select-service and full-service hotels, whose Python agent assembles annual energy and emissions reports for lenders and brand standards
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
top_tasks: Report energy and water cost per occupied room by hotel
Translate a utility-savings retrofit into NOI and value for the owner
Prepare year-end energy and emissions disclosures for lenders
hardest_task: A 290-key downtown Chicago hotel ran 70.1% occupancy at $160 ADR on $16.9M of total revenue; a $3.1M controls-and-boiler retrofit is modelled to cut utility spend by $420k a year. The agent must show the owner the NOI and value impact at an 8.5% cap rate and the unlevered return, and tie the energy savings back to a USALI-style P&L.
data_it_needs: USALI KPIs (occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, GOPPAR), cap-rate value math, ideally Chicago energy benchmarking data per building
dealbreakers: Output that mislabels USALI lines; silent unit mistakes (room-nights versus rooms); no way to pull Chicago benchmark data
budget_note: Sustainability tooling is a small line item; would not pay for anything that Excel already does.

role: CRE lender and debt underwriting agent
deployer: The credit-underwriting group of a fictional institutional life-company lender with a Texas student-housing book, whose Custom GPT drafts the sizing and structure section of credit memos
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
top_tasks: Size a refinance under LTV, DSCR and debt-yield tests with downside stresses
Build the amortization schedule with an IO period for the term sheet
Estimate prepayment cost on the existing loan so the borrower knows the all-in refinance cost
hardest_task: A borrower asks for the largest refinance of a 612-bed purpose-built student-housing property near the Austin campus: NOI $4.185M, appraised $64.4M, existing balance $36.4M with 38 months left at 4.35%. The agent must size at 65% LTV, 1.25x DSCR and an 8.5% debt yield at 6.2% on a 30-year schedule, run NOI down 5-20% with rates up 50-100 bps and a 10% value cut, and estimate the prepayment premium on the old loan.
data_it_needs: Loan sizing and stress calculators, amortization with IO and actual/360, prepayment and yield maintenance; ideally comps and CMBS or recorded-mortgage data for Austin student housing
dealbreakers: Sizing that disagrees with the lender's template; hidden convention differences; the Custom GPT being unable to call the prepayment calculator
budget_note: Institutional budget exists but is approved per vendor; a free tier is fine for a pilot, paid only with an SLA and invoicing.

role: CRE lender and debt underwriting agent
deployer: The credit team of a fictional institutional healthcare-focused bank lender in the Bay Area that runs a Python underwriting agent over borrower packages
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
top_tasks: Spread the borrower's T-12 onto our chart of accounts and tie to the stated NOI
Size the loan on underwritten NOI under LTV, DSCR and debt-yield tests
Cost the existing loan's defeasance so the borrower sees refinance economics
hardest_task: A borrower sends a PDF-extracted T-12 for a 78,000 SF Oakland-area medical plaza: EGI $3.81M, NOI $2.466M, reserves $42k. The agent must spread every line with the quote and page, show that the totals foot, size a refinance on NOI after reserves at 6.35% over 25 years against a $41.4M value (60% LTV, 1.30x DSCR, 8.5% debt yield), and cost defeasance on an $18.2M existing loan with 54 months left and a stepped Treasury curve plus $185k of costs.
data_it_needs: Cited T-12 spreading with footing checks, loan sizing, defeasance cost; Alameda and San Francisco recorded-mortgage data would help but is secondary
dealbreakers: Spread that silently drops or reclassifies lines; numbers without citations; a REST surface that changes shape between tools
budget_note: Bank procurement needs a vendor review; a $49 key is a credit-card purchase an analyst can expense, a $599 team plan needs sign-off.

deployer: A fictional mid-market South Florida multifamily owner with eleven garden and mid-rise communities, whose Custom GPT gives property managers a monthly rent-roll review
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
top_tasks: Monthly rent-roll review: GPR, loss to lease, concessions, economic occupancy
Lease-expiration ladder and renewal-pricing review
Compare effective rent after concessions across floor plans
hardest_task: A 240-unit Miami-Dade garden community is running 93% physical occupancy but concessions of four to six weeks free are being used on 18% of new leases and 12 units sit on notice; the asset manager needs GPR, loss to lease, amortised concessions and economic occupancy as of the rent-roll date, and a 12-month expiration ladder, all of which must tie to Yardi to within a few dollars.
data_it_needs: A rent-roll analysis tool with stated conventions (weeks-free valuation, concession amortisation, notice units), unit-level output, and ideally Miami-Dade owner and sales data
dealbreakers: Differences from Yardi that cannot be explained; unflagged treatment of notice or month-to-month units; GPT import failures
budget_note: Yardi already holds the rent roll; would pay only if the monthly review is cheaper than analyst time, and not per-property.

deployer: The acquisitions group of a fictional institutional industrial REIT with a Central Texas logistics platform, using a Claude Desktop connector to pre-screen bulk and multi-tenant distribution deals before a human underwrites in ARGUS
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
top_tasks: Pre-screen a multi-tenant industrial rent roll with a 5-year DCF
Check WALT and rollover exposure on the in-place roll
Model a JV equity waterfall with a tiered promote
hardest_task: A 640,000 SF multi-tenant distribution campus off the SH-130 corridor is offered at $66.5M with six suites: two NNN anchors, a base-year manufacturer, a gross e-commerce tenant, a 60,000 SF vacancy and a small-bay suite in free rent. The agent has to run a 5-year mid-year DCF with a 5.75% exit cap and 7.5% discount rate, report WALT, and split the equity 90/10 LP/GP through an 8% pref and two IRR-hurdle tiers.
data_it_needs: A DCF whose rollover, recovery and mid-year conventions can be re-performed; WALT; equity waterfall; Austin-area industrial comps and recorded sales
dealbreakers: A rollover model that silently disagrees with the roll; inputs in the wrong unit accepted without a flag; no way to reproduce outputs independently
budget_note: The group already licenses ARGUS and CoStar; a new tool must save a screening step, and the committee will not approve an unaudited calculator.

deployer: A fictional mid-market Chicago lab and R&D landlord whose lease-admin team uses a Custom GPT to abstract leases and amendments and to check tenant estoppels before refinancings
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
top_tasks: Abstract a lab lease and its amendments into a current-state record with citations
Compare tenant estoppel statements with the controlling lease terms
Maintain critical dates (expiration, renewal notice, rent steps) in the lease system
hardest_task: A 18,400 RSF third-floor lab lease (10 years from 2024-04-01, three rent steps from $62.00 to $65.78, 14.5% share, 5% non-cumulative cap on controllables, one five-year renewal at 95% of FMV) was amended in June 2026 to extend the term to 2037, raise the share to 16.8% and reset rent to $68.10. The agent must produce the current abstract with amendment precedence and then test a lender estoppel that states a 15.8% share and $66.20 rent.
data_it_needs: A verifier that confirms every extracted term is really on the cited page, amendment precedence, and an estoppel-to-lease comparison; the extraction itself is the agent's job
dealbreakers: Terms accepted without a quote check; amendments applied in the wrong order; no way to see why something was rejected
budget_note: Lease-admin tooling is bought per document volume; a free verifier on top of our existing abstraction workflow is welcome, but we would not pay until it handled our PDFs.

role: Corporate occupier and real estate portfolio agent
deployer: The corporate real estate team of a fictional institutional biotech company with 62,000 SF of lab and office space on Seattle's Eastside and in the Lake Union area, running a TypeScript agent that supports lease decisions and lease accounting
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
top_tasks: Compare landlord proposals for lab space on one effective-cost basis
Decide between renewing in place and relocating
Remeasure lease liability and ROU asset after a modification (ASC 842)
hardest_task: The company's 62,000 SF lab lease expires in mid-2027. It has three 10-year proposals ($64.50 to $96.00 per RSF with free rent of 4 to 8 months, TI of $90 to $140 per RSF and different opex structures: NNN, base year) and a renewal at $74.50. The agent must rank the proposals, test renew versus relocate over a 120-month horizon including $16.1M of build-out, 3 months of downtime and 2 months of double rent, and then remeasure the ASC 842 liability for a modification that extends an existing lease.
data_it_needs: Discounted effective-cost comparison with stated conventions, renew-vs-relocate break-even, ASC 842 remeasurement table that foots; Seattle comps would help
dealbreakers: Conventions that cannot be reproduced in our model; undisclosed timing (arrears vs advance); results that cannot be audited by accounting
budget_note: Corporate real-estate technology is bought through a procurement process; a free open-source calculator is approved faster than a paid one, and finance will want to re-perform every number.

deployer: A fictional four-person Los Angeles investment-sales boutique specializing in grocery-anchored neighbourhood centers, using a Claude Desktop connector to prepare offering-memorandum financials and buyer Q&A
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
top_tasks: Price a listing: direct-cap value and implied cap rate with below-the-line adjustments
Check percentage rent and breakpoints on the anchor and major shops
Collect shop-space lease comps and screen buyer questions about anchor exclusives
hardest_task: A 118,000 SF grocery-anchored center in West LA is going to market at $62.5M (5.33% on NOI after reserves). The broker's agent must defend the cap rate with below-the-line adjustments (free rent burn-off, lease-up, a $450k roof), compute the grocer's overage rent on $56.3M of sales, add a recent shop-space comp with net effective rent to the pricing package, and tell a buyer's agent whether an urgent-care clinic with a pharmacy would hit the anchor's exclusive.
data_it_needs: Direct-cap and percentage-rent math, comp validation and NER, exclusive-use screening; ideally Los Angeles retail comps and recorded sales
dealbreakers: A wrong or unflagged number in a buyer-facing OM; anything that implies legal advice on exclusives; no market comps
budget_note: Brokerage tech budget is small and already spent on CoStar and LoopNet; a free tool that saves an analyst hour per listing is welcome, but we would not pay for a tool without market comps.
